questions.prompt: What practical decision should this formalization help us make?
questions.why: It prevents a technically precise answer to the wrong business question.
A formalizer or provider cannot invent domain authority.

questions.prompt: What must this work not claim?
questions.why: The ceiling prevents proof, runtime, security, and release claims from collapsing together.

questions.prompt: What must be true in normal domain language?
questions.why: The business statement remains readable without formal notation.

questions.prompt: Give at least one example that must pass and one that must not pass.
questions.why: Examples expose hidden ambiguity before formal syntax is selected.

questions.prompt: Which types and predicates carry the rule?
questions.why: Every quantified or compared thing needs a stable interpretation.

questions.prompt: Which facts must be current at decision time?
questions.why: Authorization and other decisions can change when time or currentness is implicit.

questions.prompt: Could an always-allow, always-deny, or empty model satisfy the words accidentally?
questions.why: A vacuous proposition can look rigorous while proving nothing useful.

steps.label: Create one exact FormalClaim source

questions.prompt: Which formal language profile expresses the meaning without hiding a load-bearing rule?
questions.why: Profile semantics are part of claim identity.
There must be one authoritative proposition, not one per provider.

questions.prompt: Which example, counterexample, or assumption would falsify this translation?
questions.why: This is the smallest semantic drift check before TDE or EVF.

steps.output_contract: FormalClaimSource/v3 Candidate plus explicit FormalClaimSourcePayload/v2 projection when TDE intake is required
